questions.questionTextEn: What was the policy of Indian National Congress during IInd World War?
questions.questionTextHi: द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस की नीति क्या थी?
optionsEn: Cooperation of Britain in the case of assurance of Complete Independence.
optionsHi: पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता के आश्वासन के मामले में ब्रिटेन का सहयोग।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). When World War II broke out in 1939, Britain made India belligerent without consulting Indian elected councils and also declared the Emergency. That action angered Indian ofﬁ cials and prompted the Congress Party to declare that India would not support the War until it had been granted Complete Independence.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) 1939 में जब द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध छिड़ गया, तो ब्रिटेन ने भारतीय निर्वाचित परिषदों से परामर्श किए बिना भारत को लड़ाकू बना दिया और आपातकाल की भी घोषणा कर दी। उस कार्रवाई से भारतीय अधिकारी नाराज हो गए और कांग्रेस पार्टी को यह घोषणा करने के लिए प्रेरित किया कि भारत तब तक युद्ध का समर्थन नहीं करेगा जब तक उसे पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता नहीं मिल जाती।

questions.questionTextEn: Statement (S) :Indian National Congress had collabo- rated/assisted British in IInd World War. Reason (R) : Because they were expecting to complete independence. Code :
questions.questionTextHi: कथन (एस): भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध में ब्रिटिशों का सहयोग/सहायता की थी। कारण (आर): क्योंकि वे पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता की उम्मीद कर रहे थे। कोड :
optionsEn: (S) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (S).
optionsHi: (एस) और (आर) व्यक्तिगत रूप से सत्य हैं, और (आर) (एस) का सही स्पष्टीकरण है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). During the Second World War the proposal approved by Indian National Congress criticized Nazism, Fascism and the Nazi invasion of Poland. It was declared under the proposal that Indian could not take part in any such war which is being fought to protect the democratic liberty, while itself being deprived of liberty. Therefore, both the statement and the reason are incorrect.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस द्वारा अनुमोदित प्रस्ताव में नाजीवाद, फासीवाद और पोलैंड पर नाजी आक्रमण की आलोचना की गई थी। प्रस्ताव के तहत यह घोषित किया गया कि भारतीय ऐसे किसी भी युद्ध में भाग नहीं ले सकते जो लोकतांत्रिक स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा के लिए लड़ा जा रहा हो, जबकि स्वयं स्वतंत्रता से वंचित हो। इसलिए, कथन और कारण दोनों गलत हैं।

questions.questionTextEn: Assertion (A) :The Congress Ministries in all the provinces resigned in the year 1939. Reason (R) : The Congress did not accept the decision of the Viceroy to declare war against Germany in the context of the Second World War. Code:
questions.questionTextHi: दावा (ए): सभी प्रांतों में कांग्रेस मंत्रिमंडलों ने वर्ष 1939 में इस्तीफा दे दिया। कारण (आर): कांग्रेस ने द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के संदर्भ में जर्मनी के खिलाफ युद्ध की घोषणा करने के वायसराय के फैसले को स्वीकार नहीं किया। कोड:
optionsEn: (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
optionsHi: (ए) और (आर) व्यक्तिगत रूप से सत्य हैं, और (आर) (ए) का सही स्पष्टीकरण है।
(ए) और (आर) व्यक्तिगत रूप से सत्य हैं, लेकिन (आर) (ए) का सही स्पष्टीकरण नहीं है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). On October 17, 1939 Lord Linlithgow declared India in the war against Germany. Congress cabinets had resigned from all the provinces for declaring war without the consent of the Congress Ministries. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) 17 अक्टूबर, 1939 को लॉर्ड लिनलिथगो ने जर्मनी के विरुद्ध भारत को युद्ध की घोषणा कर दी। कांग्रेस मंत्रिमंडलों की सहमति के बिना युद्ध की घोषणा करने के कारण सभी प्रांतों से कांग्रेस मंत्रिमंडलों ने इस्तीफा दे दिया था। अतः, विकल्प (ए) सही उत्तर है।

questions.questionTextEn: The Congress Ministries in all the provinces resigned in the year 1939, because :
questions.questionTextHi: वर्ष 1939 में सभी प्रांतों में कांग्रेस मंत्रिमंडलों ने इस्तीफा दे दिया, क्योंकि:
optionsEn: Congress was unable to make a cabinet in other four provinces.
The rise of the left wing of Congress made impossible to work for the cabinet.
There was too much communal turbulence in the provinces
None of the above is true from the given statement (a), (b), (c).
optionsHi: अन्य चार प्रांतों में कांग्रेस मंत्रिमंडल बनाने में असमर्थ रही।
कांग्रेस के वामपंथी दल के उदय ने मंत्रिमंडल के लिए काम करना असंभव बना दिया।
प्रांतों में बहुत अधिक सांप्रदायिक अशांति थी
उपरोक्त में से कोई भी दिए गए कथन (ए), (बी), (सी) से सत्य नहीं है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). After 28 months of tenure, the cabinets of Congress resigned in 1939 because British Government had declared India as a war-torn country without the consent of Indians. Thus, option (d) is true.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) 28 महीने के कार्यकाल के बाद 1939 में कांग्रेस के मंत्रिमंडलों ने इस्तीफा दे दिया क्योंकि ब्रिटिश सरकार ने भारतीयों की सहमति के बिना भारत को युद्धग्रस्त देश घोषित कर दिया था। इस प्रकार, विकल्प (डी) सत्य है।

questions.questionTextHi: द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान ब्रिटेन के ब्रिटिश प्रधान मंत्री कौन थे?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). Winston Churchill was the Prime Minister of Britain during IInd World War. His tenure was from 1940-45 and 1951-55. Demand for Pakistan *The idea of a separate homeland for Muslims was ﬁ rstly proposed by Iqbal in Allahabad Session (1930) of Muslim League in his presidential address. Whereas the word ‘Pakistan / PAKSTAN’ was ﬁ rstly used by a student named Chaudhary Rehmat Ali in 1933 in his pamphlet “Now or Never ; Are we to live or Perish for ever?”. *This name was prepared from the ﬁ ve British India’s North Units. These units were - Punjab, North-West Frontier Province (Afghan Province) Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan. From 22 to 24 March, 1940, the Muslim League held its session in Lahore which was chaired by Md. Ali Jinnah. In this session a separate Muslim nation out of India was demanded. In this session, Jinnah said that he would not accept anything less than a separate Muslim Country. *Sarojini Naidu termed Jinnah as an Ambassador of Hindu- Muslim unity. Jawahar Lal Nehru in his book The Discovery of India, mentioned that Iqbal in a meeting said that "Jinnah is a politician, you are a patriot". *Two Nation theory of Jinnah was accepted in the Lahore Session of Muslim League which was held in March 1940. This proposal was drafted by Sikandar Hayat Khan and was presented by Fazlul Haq on 23rd March, 1940. To commemorate this day 23rd March, of 1943 was celebrated as Pakistan Day. 1. Who among the following had primarily used the word ‘Pakistan’ for separate State for Indian Muslims? (a) Sir Mohammad Iqbal (b) Sir Aga Khan (c) M. A. Jinnah (d) Chaudhary Rehmat Ali and his friends R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1996 Ans. (d) The word Pakistan/PAKSTAN was primarily used by the student of Cambridge University Chaudhary Rehmat Ali in his letter entitled “Now or Never; Are we to live or Perish for Ever?” 2. Who among the following first coined the word 'Pakistan'? (a) Mohammad Ali Jinnah (b) Choudhary Rehmat Ali (c) Syed Ahmad Khan (d) Mohammad Ashfaq Khan M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023 Ans. (b) The term "Pakistan" or Pakstan was ﬁ rst coined by Choudhary Rahmat Ali, a Pakistani nationalist in a pamphlet published in 1933. The word formed by combining the name of the regions that were to constitute the proposed nation: Punjab, Afghan Province (North-West Frontier Province), Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan. The Idea of Pakistan gained further momentum, leading to the creation of the independent state of Pakistan in 1947. 3. Demand for Pakistan *The idea of a separate homeland for Muslims was ﬁ rstly proposed by Iqbal in Allahabad Session (1930) of Muslim League in his presidential address. Whereas the word ‘Pakistan / PAKSTAN’ was ﬁ rstly used by a student named Chaudhary Rehmat Ali in 1933 in his pamphlet “Now or Never ; Are we to live or Perish for ever?”. *This name was prepared from the ﬁ ve British India’s North Units. These units were - Punjab, North-West Frontier Province (Afghan Province) Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan. From 22 to 24 March, 1940, the Muslim League held its session in Lahore which was chaired by Md. Ali Jinnah. In this session a separate Muslim nation out of India was demanded. In this session, Jinnah said that he would not accept anything less than a separate Muslim Country. *Sarojini Naidu termed Jinnah as an Ambassador of Hindu- Muslim unity. Jawahar Lal Nehru in his book The Discovery of India, mentioned that Iqbal in a meeting said that "Jinnah is a politician, you are a patriot". *Two Nation theory of Jinnah was accepted in the Lahore Session of Muslim League which was held in March 1940. This proposal was drafted by Sikandar Hayat Khan and was presented by Fazlul Haq on 23rd March, 1940. To commemorate this day 23rd March, of 1943 was celebrated as Pakistan Day. 1. Jinnah (d) Chaudhary Rehmat Ali and his friends R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1996 Ans. (d) The word Pakistan/PAKSTAN was primarily used by the student of Cambridge University Chaudhary Rehmat Ali in his letter entitled “Now or Never; Are we to live or Perish for Ever?” 2. Who among the following first coined the word 'Pakistan'? (a) Mohammad Ali Jinnah (b) Choudhary Rehmat Ali (c) Syed Ahmad Khan (d) Mohammad Ashfaq Khan M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023 Ans. (b) The term "Pakistan" or Pakstan was ﬁ rst coined by Choudhary Rahmat Ali, a Pakistani nationalist in a pamphlet published in 1933. The word formed by combining the name of the regions that were to constitute the proposed nation: Punjab, Afghan Province (North-West Frontier Province), Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan.
